Spell Index approaches the portfolio as a practitioner's reference work — a personal grimoire organized into clearly indexed sections, each spell entry standing in for a project, skill, or piece of experience. The design is orderly and legible by intention, with refined mystical details woven through the typography and layout without disrupting the catalog structure.

## Theme Overview

Spell Index takes inspiration from medieval grimoires and indexed magical catalogs to create a portfolio structure that is genuinely organized and scannable. Rather than building around atmosphere alone, the layout uses clear section headings, catalogued entries, and refined typographic hierarchy to make content easy to navigate. The mystical details appear in the ornamentation, the section labels, and the subtle decorative elements — present enough to establish identity, restrained enough not to overwhelm the content.

## Design Highlights

- Grimoire-inspired catalog structure with indexed sections and clearly delineated content entries
- Searchable or browsable layout that prioritizes content legibility alongside magical atmosphere
- Refined mystical typographic details in headings, labels, and decorative dividers
- Dark but structured palette that balances occult mood with clear information hierarchy
- Modular entry format that works naturally for projects, skills, and experience sections

## Who This Theme Suits

Spell Index is ideal for developers who have a lot of content to share and want a portfolio that visitors can actually navigate rather than scroll through. The catalog format works especially well for those with deep project histories, varied technical skills, or writing and open-source contributions they want to surface in an organized way.

<Note>The spell-catalog metaphor is flexible — the entry format adapts naturally to any kind of portfolio content, from projects and blog posts to talks, tools, and technical guides.</Note>
